Good morning,

Today is 19 September 2026.

This is Day 1 of your SSC CHSL 2026 preparation system.

You have already applied for the Staff Selection Commission Combined Higher Secondary (10+2) Level Examination, 2026.

This is the Day 1 foundation pack in the same permanent-command format used by the later Daily Command Sheet. It is a historical Day 1 record, preserved so the preparation system can distinguish original work from later revision.

WHAT to do today: solve every NEW question before checking answers, record attempted/correct/wrong/skipped/time, study the computer notes, complete the 10-minute typing task, complete the fitness routine where appropriate, and record what needs revision.
WHERE to verify: official SSC notices, SATHEE SSC, PIB and the listed free resources.
WHEN to do it: use the study blocks in the daily command workflow and complete the end-of-day report before sleep.

6. COMPUTER KNOWLEDGE - TODAY'S STUDY NOTES
Computer Fundamentals
A computer follows an input-process-output cycle. Data enters through input devices, the CPU processes instructions, and output devices
present results. Core hardware includes the CPU, memory, storage and input/output peripherals. Learn the difference between volatile
memory (RAM) and non-volatile storage.
Hardware
Hardware means physical components you can touch. Examples: motherboard, CPU, RAM, SSD/HDD, keyboard, mouse, monitor and
printer. CPU performance depends on architecture, clock speed, cores and workload. SSDs generally offer faster access than HDDs
because they have no moving magnetic platters.
Software
System software runs and manages the computer; application software helps users perform tasks. An operating system is system
software. A word processor, spreadsheet and web browser are applications. Know the difference between open-source and proprietary
software.
Operating Systems
An operating system manages hardware, files, processes, users and applications. Windows provides tools such as File Explorer and
Task Manager. Learn basic file operations, folders, extensions, copy/cut/paste, and the purpose of keyboard shortcuts.
Internet
The internet is a global network of interconnected networks. A web browser retrieves web resources using protocols such as HTTPS.
Learn the difference between a website, webpage, URL, browser, search engine, download and upload.
Networking
A LAN covers a small local area; a WAN covers larger geographic areas. Routers connect networks and forward packets. Switches
connect devices within a LAN. Know basic terms: IP address, MAC address, bandwidth, latency and DNS.
Cybersecurity
Common threats include phishing, malware, ransomware, spyware and Trojan horses. Use unique passwords, multi-factor authentication,
software updates and caution with links or attachments. Never treat an unsolicited login page as trustworthy merely because it looks
professional.
Word Processing
Learn document creation, text formatting, alignment, margins, headings, page breaks, tables, find/replace, spell-check and keyboard
shortcuts. Practice Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+S and Ctrl+F.
Spreadsheets
A spreadsheet uses rows and columns. A cell is identified by a reference such as B4. Formulae begin with =. Learn SUM, AVERAGE,
MAX, MIN, COUNT, relative references and simple sorting/filtering.
Presentations
Presentation software organizes information into slides. Learn slide layouts, themes, text boxes, images, charts, transitions and presenter
mode. Good slides communicate one main idea clearly rather than filling the page with dense text.
Digital Awareness
Know safe email practices, digital payments, OTP confidentiality, backups, cloud storage, digital signatures and basic privacy hygiene.
Treat OTPs and passwords as confidential authentication data and never share them with callers claiming to be officials.
7. TYPING TEST - DAY 1
LDC/JSA practice passage - type continuously for 10 minutes. Today's target is accuracy first; do not chase speed by making errors.
The current CHSL typing standard commonly used for LDC/JSA is 35 wpm in English or 30 wpm in Hindi, with the selected medium
treated as final. Verify the 2026 notice for the exact post-specific rule.
Public administration depends on accurate records, timely communication and careful handling of information. A clerk may need to
prepare letters, update registers, enter data, organize files and respond to routine requests. Speed matters, but accuracy matters first
because a small typing error can change a name, date, number or official instruction. During practice, sit comfortably, keep your wrists
relaxed and look at the screen rather than the keyboard whenever possible. Complete the passage without unnecessary pauses and
record your final error count.
